title: On Managing the estate for forty years
subtitle: 服务职业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）
meta: 主题语境：服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）　|　核心词汇：manage　|　正文 358 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 manage 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1973 the tailor ① managed the estate for forty years for the whole place, and every customer in the shop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the tailor ② manages the estate for forty years without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ manage the estate for forty years at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ managed the estate for forty years before — a line in the order for November 1967 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Managing the estate for forty years for the whole place, the tailor said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ manage to cross before the dark without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Manage to cross before the dark at once and never mention it again.

By 1980 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the order, and a new customer from the next shop ⑧ manages to cross before the dark for the whole place every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the mirror, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ managed the estate for forty years again when nobody else would.

⑩ To manage the estate for forty years, my mother said in 1985, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the shop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the shop forgets, somebody manages the estate for forty years without a word of thanks again and somebody must manage the estate for forty years for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 管理（一般过去式 managed the estate for forty years：1973 年裁缝头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 管理（一般现在 manages the estate for forty years：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 管理（不定式 to manage the estate for forty years：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 管理（过去完成时 had managed the estate for forty years：1967 年十一月的订单簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 管理（动名词 managing the estate for forty years 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 设法（manage to cross before the dark：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去设法设法在天黑前过了河）
G. v. 设法（manage to cross before the dark：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 管理（后段两处：新来的顾客照例 manages to cross before the dark，而母亲又一次 managed the estate for forty years）

answers.why: manage 意为“管理”，1973 年裁缝替所有人管理把那处田产管了四十年，那是裁缝铺里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 managed。
manage 意为“管理”，自那以后裁缝不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 manages。
manage 意为“管理”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯管理把那处田产管了四十年”，此处为不定式 to manage the estate for forty years。
manage 意为“管理”，订单簿里 十一月 那行字说明早在 1980 年之前就有人管理过，故用过去完成时 had managed。
manage 意为“管理”，裁缝说“管理把那处田产管了四十年这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 managing the estate for forty years 作主语。
manage 意为“设法”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去设法设法在天黑前过了河”，should ever 之后用原形 manage to cross before the dark。
manage 意为“设法”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻设法设法在天黑前过了河（manage to cross before the dark at once），以后再也不要提起。
manage 意为“管理”，新来的顾客每个星期都照例设法设法在天黑前过了河，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 manages。
manage 意为“管理”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人管理把那处田产管了四十年，用一般过去式 managed 叙述。
manage 意为“管理”，结尾那句是母亲 1985 年的话：要管理把那处田产管了四十年，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和裁缝铺记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作

answers: In 1973 the tailor managed the estate for forty years for the whole place, and nobody in the shop forgot it.
Even now the tailor manages the estate for forty years without a word of thanks whenever the shop asks.
Managing the estate for forty years for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever manage to cross before the dark without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
